claims.text: KRAS G12C is a frequent, poor-prognosis driver mutation in NSCLC

links.quote: found in approximately 14% of NSCLC cases and associated with poor prognosis

claims.text: Divarasib occupies the same switch-II pocket as sotorasib and adagrasib but holds the loop in a different conformation
No human genetic evidence on the effect of losing KRAS function is in the bundle, so the direction of action cannot be checked against genetics
Divarasib is in a randomized Phase 3 trial against sotorasib or adagrasib in KRAS G12C-positive advanced non-small cell lung cancer

links.quote: assess the safety and efficacy of divarasib compared to locally approved KRAS G12C inhibitors (sotorasib or adagrasib)

claims.text: The Phase 3 primary endpoint is progression-free survival judged by blinded independent central review

links.quote: blinded independent central review (BICR) according to RECIST v1.1

claims.text: Roche reports that the Phase 3 trial met its primary and key secondary endpoints, progression-free and overall survival

links.quote: The study met its primary and key secondary endpoint

claims.text: In the Phase 1 study divarasib gave a confirmed response in 53.4% of patients with non-small cell lung cancer

links.quote: a confirmed response was observed in 53.4% of patients

claims.text: Treatment-related adverse events were frequent in the Phase 1 study, with grade 3 events in 11% of patients

links.quote: Treatment-related adverse events occurred in 127 patients (93%)

claims.text: The approved G12C inhibitors set the bar divarasib must beat: sotorasib and adagrasib each improved median progression-free survival over docetaxel

links.quote: statistically significant increase in the progression-free survival for sotorasib

claims.text: The size of the Phase 3 benefit (hazard ratios, median progression-free and overall survival) is not in the evidence: the company release gives no numbers
No failed trial of another drug against the same target in this indication is in the bundle, so whether similar programs failed is not shown

The wider competitive landscape (other KRAS G12C and RAS(ON) programs, other mechanisms in this indication, discontinued programs) was not searched, so competitors beyond the two approved inhibitors are unknown
Divarasib binds KRAS G12C in the allosteric switch-II pocket

links.quote: binds in the same allosteric pocket as sotorasib and adagrasib

claims.text: Whether the exposure reached in patients is the effective one is not shown in the available evidence
Target engagement in tumour tissue is not shown; response in patients does not prove it
Divarasib produces confirmed responses in patients with KRAS G12C NSCLC

links.quote: a confirmed response was observed in 53.4% of patients

claims.text: Divarasib improved progression-free and overall survival over the approved KRAS G12C inhibitors in a randomised phase 3, as reported by the sponsor

links.quote: statistically significant improvements in both progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS)

claims.text: Treatment-related adverse events were mostly low grade in the phase 1 study

objections.objection: The registry still lists the trial as active with no posted results, so the benefit over the approved inhibitors rests on a company press release alone.

questions.text: Is the exposure divarasib reaches in tumour tissue the exposure that worked in the laboratory? Ask the sponsor for tumour pharmacokinetics.
Is KRAS G12C engaged in patients' tumours at the doses given? Ask for paired biopsies or circulating tumour DNA data.
What are the hazard ratios and the overall survival in the Phase 3 trial? The press release gives no numbers.
Has any other drug against KRAS failed in lung cancer for lack of efficacy? Ask a clinician who ran such trials.
Does human genetics say anything about losing KRAS function?

judgments.reason: a trial status says nothing about the size of the benefit
